paragraphs: For the proposed survey, students first drew a boundary around the places they intended to include. They listed shops on side streets as well as the official stalls, and asked businesses to separate festival visitors from regular customers where possible. A shop's total sales could not automatically be counted as festival spending. Nor could reports of more customers establish how much each person had spent. The students wanted the next set of figures to answer a clearly defined question rather than simply look more complete.

They also checked how the previous year's figures had been collected. If the new survey covered more businesses, its total could rise even without a change in visitor behavior. The report therefore proposed keeping the old stall measure alongside the broader estimate for one year. Readers would be able to see what had changed in the method before comparing the totals. Expanding a measure was useful only if its new boundaries were explained. A larger number alone would not show whether the festival had brought more money into the village.
rationale: 部分指標と全体の推論を区別し、比較年度の測定範囲変更を検討する。関係節、過去完了、nor倒置、間接疑問を扱う。

paragraphs: During one practice session, a visitor asked why two similar objects had different storage instructions. The trainee could describe the materials listed on the labels, but did not know the reason for the difference. She explained that limit and offered to ask the staff member responsible for the museum's collections. Instead of guessing from the objects' appearance, she wrote down the question and checked how the visitor could receive a reply. The supervisor praised the way she had kept the question open without turning an uncertain idea into a fact.

At the next scheduled training meeting, trainees compared the questions they had referred to staff. Some revealed gaps in the training notes, while others required information beyond a guide's role. The museum revised one explanation and added a clear contact route for specialist questions. It did not expect volunteers to become experts on every subject. It expected them to prepare carefully, notice when their knowledge was insufficient, and connect visitors with an appropriate next step. Being honest about a limit worked best when it was accompanied by practical help.
rationale: 事実の準備と知識の限界への対応を両立する。受動態、省略、間接疑問、動名詞主語と専門照会の手順を扱う。

paragraphs: Before the paper reports were stopped, the committee tested one monthly summary against the information teachers actually used. It discovered that a calendar entry could describe a planned meeting without showing whether it had taken place. A list of plans was not automatically a record of attendance. The clubs therefore added a brief confirmation after each session, including whether the meeting had been canceled. This gave the summary a clearer basis without requiring students to write the entire report again.

For the first month, a teacher and two club members checked a sample of summaries together. They found that one heading was unclear and changed it before the system was extended to all clubs. The school also recorded who would correct an entry when a mistake was found. This check included both practical clarity and responsibility for corrections. Reducing repeated work did not mean allowing errors to pass unnoticed. By checking the information rather than defending a particular medium, the committee could preserve the old purpose while improving the way people carried it out.
rationale: 規則の目的と媒体を区別し、予定と実施の差も確認する。関係節、受動態、形式主語、間接疑問と分詞表現を扱う。

paragraphs: To test the new arrangement, staff gave three first-time users short examples of problems and asked where they would begin. One person looking for help with a damaged notice chose an unexpected heading. Her explanation showed that two headings sounded almost identical outside the organization. Staff changed the wording and repeated the task with a new reader, rather than telling the first person that she should have known the intended difference.

They also added a visible way to contact the center when no heading seemed suitable. That route remained available even when the online categories changed. Common situations could guide many visitors, but could not describe every unusual case. The page was meant to support contact, not make help conditional on choosing the right category.

At later reviews, the team examined unsuccessful searches as well as popular links. A high number of clicks could mean interest, but might also mean that people were moving between pages without finding an answer. Short observations of actual use helped staff distinguish those possibilities. The center kept accurate answers and continued checking the routes by which people reached them.
rationale: 情報の正確さと発見可能性を区別する。関係節、仮定的推量、過去完了、動名詞と指標の複数解釈を扱う。

paragraphs: After seeing the display, one shopper asked which bag had traveled the shorter distance. The diagram identified the places used in production, but did not include every journey between them. The student marked the distance as not documented instead of estimating it from the label alone. A nearby sewing workshop did not necessarily mean that the cloth had traveled a short way. She added a note explaining what would have to be checked before making that comparison.

Another shopper cared most about keeping a bag in use for several years. He asked both sellers whether a damaged handle could be replaced and how he could contact someone about a repair. Those questions revealed information that a broad claim about local production had not supplied. The student added a repair column to her display, keeping confirmed answers separate from unanswered questions. Her aim was not to assign every bag a single score. It was to make the reasons for a choice easier to examine, while leaving room for different priorities and for information that was still missing.
rationale: 好印象の表示と工程の確認状態を区別する。省略、関係節、形式目的語、間接疑問、基準に応じた判断を扱う。
